claim: Training real-world humanoid locomotion with PPO requires 4 A100 GPUs and thousands of parallel randomized environments in Isaac Gym; exact step counts are not reported in the main paper (relegated to supplement).
stance_target: Training budget for bipedal humanoid locomotion with PPO
scope_conditions: Agility Robotics Digit humanoid (30 DoF, 45 kg); Isaac Gym; PPO; teacher-student architecture
quoted_support: We leverage fast GPU simulation powered by Isaac Gym and parallelize training across four A100 GPUs and thousands of randomized environments.

claim: A two-step teacher-student training pipeline for humanoid locomotion trains a teacher state policy with full state access first, then trains a student observation policy using PPO + imitation loss from the teacher, with the imitation loss annealed to zero at training midpoint.
stance_target: Teacher-student distillation as the standard method for observation-limited locomotion policies
scope_conditions: Digit humanoid bipedal locomotion; Isaac Gym; PPO; zero-shot sim-to-real transfer
quoted_support: The weighting factor is gradually annealed to zero over the course of the training process, typically reaching zero at the mid-point of the training horizon, which enables the observation policy to benefit from the teacher early on and learn to surpass it eventually.
numbers: λ annealed to 0 at training midpoint
